name: Fluticasone (inhaled)
contraindications: No absolute contraindications for inhaled use; caution in active untreated infections of the respiratory tract
interactions: Systemic strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole) may increase systemic exposure to fluticasone and risk systemic corticosteroid effects
monitoring: Regular review of inhaler technique and adherence; monitor for oral candidiasis and advise mouth rinsing after use; assess growth in children on high-dose ICS
pregnancy: Use if clinically indicated; balance benefits and risks and discuss with obstetric team
sideEffects: Local: oral candidiasis (thrush), dysphonia; systemic effects are rare at low-moderate inhaled doses but possible with high doses or with potent CYP3A4 inhibition
clinicalPearls: Often combined with a long-acting beta-agonist for asthma control; advise mouth rinsing after inhalation to reduce thrush; dose and device selection should be individualised
indication: Maintenance therapy for asthma; considered in COPD patients with frequent exacerbations and significant eosinophilia
